brief: A phone charging station: a closed box with a cover that lets a cable pass through.
costSource: token-equivalent at Muse Spark Open shared rates, info only: the Dedicated Endpoint bills GPU seconds while up (.spend/modal-dedicated.jsonl)

requirements.evidence: 2-cell base (piece:0,0,0;full + piece:1,0,0;full) with bottom covers (cover:0,0,0;full;bottom, cover:1,0,0;full;bottom), top covers (cover:0,0,0;full;top, cover:1,0,0;full;top) and 10 side end caps (cap:*;150/210/270/30/90 + 210/270/30/330/90) enclosing all outer faces; two cells joined by jointBolt:0#0,0#0; check_build meshClash clear, no open issues.

requirements.requirement: Cover that lets a cable pass through
requirements.evidence: Both top covers set to type cable via setCoverType (cable pass-through opening) on q0r0 and q1r0 – the opening is visible from above and the cable-coil prop sits at the pass-through; look az45 polar10 sees props, check_build clear.

requirements.requirement: Phone charging station (sized to hold a phone)
requirements.evidence: Deck f10 across the two top covers is 310x227mm, fits phone prop 147x72mm (phone lie pose on f10, prop:1) plus cable-coil (prop:2 on phone); interior headroom 68mm under top cover, exterior box ~310mm long – demonstrates use as charging station.

finish.summary: Built a 2-cell closed box (2x full bases, bottom and top covers, 10 side caps) with both top covers configured to the cable pass-through variant. The sealed enclosure is shown with a phone and coiled cable on the top deck at the cable opening, verified clear by check_build and visible in look.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
